slot.brief: Zener regulator circuit with source, series resistor, Zener voltage and load; find current through Zener and through load, and dissipated Zener power; include circuit diagram.

stem: In the Zener regulator circuit shown in the figure, Vs = 24 V, Rs = 600 ohm, Vz = 9 V, and RL = 450 ohm. The current through the Zener diode, the current through the load resistor, and the power dissipated in the Zener diode are, respectively:

verdicts.working: Assuming the Zener regulates at 9 V: the series current is (24−9)/600 = 25 mA. The load current is 9/450 = 20 mA, so the Zener current is 5 mA and its power is 9 × 5 mA = 45 mW.

working:
I_L = Vz / RL = 9 / 450 = 0.020 A = 20 mA. I_s = (Vs - Vz) / Rs = (24 - 9) / 600 = 15 / 600 = 0.025 A = 25 mA. I_z = I_s - I_L = 25 - 20 = 5 mA. P_z = Vz * I_z = 9 * 0.005 = 0.045 W = 45 mW.

Independent check: Assuming the Zener regulates at 9 V: the series current is (24−9)/600 = 25 mA. The load current is 9/450 = 20 mA, so the Zener current is 5 mA and its power is 9 × 5 mA = 45 mW.
solution:
With the Zener regulating, the load voltage is $V_z=9\,\text{V}$.
$$I_L=\frac{V_z}{R_L}=\frac{9}{450}=20\,\text{mA},\qquad I_s=\frac{V_s-V_z}{R_s}=\frac{24-9}{600}=25\,\text{mA}$$
Thus $I_z=I_s-I_L=5\,\text{mA}$ and $P_z=V_zI_z=9(0.005)=45\,\text{mW}$.

figure.description: Draw a DC voltage source Vs with positive terminal at top and negative terminal at bottom. From the positive terminal, connect a series resistor Rs horizontally to the right to a junction node A. Label this resistor Rs = 600 ohm. From node A, draw a Zener diode vertically downward back to the bottom rail, with its cathode at node A and anode at the bottom rail; label it Vz = 9 V. Also from node A, draw a load resistor RL vertically downward to the bottom rail to the right of the Zener diode; label it RL = 450 ohm. Label the source Vs = 24 V.
